summary: Battery Point Breakwater light marks the eastern entrance to Lunenburg Harbour. A light has stood on the point since 1864; the present breakwater tower dates from 1951.

access.note: Breakwater not open to the public and no public right-of-way to the light. Lighthouse Friends advises viewing the tower from a distance.

events.note: First light on Battery Point: a dwelling with a lantern room on its roof
John A. Ernst appointed in November 1864 at $240 a year
Light established in 1937. Lighthouse Friends places it near the end of the breakwater; the NSLPS describes a square wood tower on the dwelling. The sources disagree.
Present breakwater tower placed on a new breakwater, September 1951
Station officially de-staffed 19 June 1987 on the retirement of Harvey L. Huskins
Millwork and metalwork repairs; tower painted, paid for with Lunenburg Waterfront Association funds

corrections.why: The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights gives no nominal range for Battery Point Breakwater (the range column is blank), so the 13 nm in the record has no source among the pages read.
The record's 1937 is the date of a later light on the point. Lighthouse Friends and the NSLPS both date the first light on Battery Point to 1864.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's OSM value (F R) and the NSLPS's 1992 description (Fixed Red) differ from the current Canadian Coast Guard list, which gives Iso R 4s with a 7.5 m focal height. The Coast Guard list is used as the current value.

notes_for_editor: 1) The 1937 light is disputed. Lighthouse Friends places it near the end of the breakwater; the NSLPS describes a square wood tower on the keepers' dwelling and gives the 1951 tower as Battery Point III. The Canadian annual reports in the corpus end in 1924, so neither account is checked against a primary report. 2) Henry Naas: Lighthouse Friends ends his term in 1908, but the keepers' tables printed 1910, 1911 and 1912 give him at Battery Point. The 1910 entry (Naas, appointed 12 March 1897) was matched by position in the column layout, with locality then keeper; the checker should read the page images at scan pages 166 (1910 volume), 256 (1911 volume) and 242 (1912 volume). 3) Other Battery Points exist: Sydney and Louisbourg both have one in the Department's tables. The 1915 entry for a 4th-order lens at Battery point (contractor E. J. Geizer, $4,340) and the 1917 Battery point entries are not used because the printed text does not say which Battery Point they are. 4) The keeper list from Lighthouse Friends (1864 to 1896, 1922 to 1935) and the Huskins years rest on that one page; no primary report in the corpus covers them. 5) Newspaper search not run: newspapers.py covers US papers only. 6) Not ascertained: the sixth-order dioptric lens and fog bell entries that the NSLPS lists under the 1951 tower, dated 1937 and 1941; they are left out of the story because the NSLPS does not say which light they belong to. 7) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1912 table line-pairs 'Battery Point Henry Naas', which confirms Naas at Battery Point that year; the 1910 date (Mar. 12, 1897) and the 1911 pairing are matched by column position. The archive.org page images (scan pages 166, 256) could not be opened from the browser pane (access denied), so the 1910 date is checked against the OCR and the 1911 and 1912 pairings only. 8) The NSLPS general description (22 ft / 6.7 m elevation) and its own details (25 ft) are both now stated in the story; the Coast Guard entry for No. 438 is on the cited page and was checked there.
